macro_events.title: US-Iran exchange fire in Strait of Hormuz, fragile ceasefire fraying
macro_events.causal_chain: US and Iran each claim the other initiated fire on shipping in Hormuz overnight — Iran says US targeted two ships entering the strait — ceasefire MOU not yet finalized → crude futures gap higher Asia session, Brent +1.20% to $101.26, WTI +0.88-1.85% to $95.64-96.66 → war-risk insurance premiums on VLCCs reprice higher, which directly capitalizes Frontline/DHT/INSW fleet → Asian refiners begin pricing partial Cape of Good Hope reroute (+12-14 days, +$2M/voyage) → Qatari LNG to Europe via Hormuz at risk, supports Dutch TTF gas → US 10Y yield held 4.34% as the move was capped by ceasefire-still-alive headlines from Trump → if a single tanker is hit overnight Sunday, expect Brent to gap $108-112 on Monday open and ES futures -1.5-2% reflex.
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Strait of Hormuz carries ~21% of global oil trade and ~20% of LNG; primary sufferers are Asian importers (China, India, Japan, South Korea), Eurozone gas consumers, and oil-importing EM (Turkey, India, Indonesia); primary beneficiaries are US shale (energy independence), Russian Urals (premium widens), and Western-flagged tanker operators capturing war-risk surcharge.
macro_events.historical_analog: September 2019 Abqaiq/Khurais drone attack: Brent +15% in 24h before retracing; the lasting trade was tanker rates +20-35% in one week as insurers raised JWC premiums; defense underperformed expectations because the conflict didn't escalate to munition consumption. Pattern fits today's tape — defense is down 13-18% in 3 months despite the ongoing conflict.
macro_events.counterargument: Trump publicly insisted ceasefire remains in effect; both sides are still negotiating a 1-page 14-point MOU per Pakistan-mediated channel; Emkay and other sell-side desks expect Hormuz reopens within weeks regardless of the noise. If MOU is signed this weekend, Brent retraces to $92-94, tanker stocks give back 6-8%, airlines and discretionary catch a 2-3% rally.

macro_events.title: April Nonfarm Payrolls release at 8:30 AM ET — consensus 55-67k, U-rate 4.3%
macro_events.causal_chain: BLS releases April employment situation at 8:30 AM ET — expected 55-67k jobs (range 55k bottom, 67k top) versus 178k March, with unemployment unchanged at 4.3% → if print hits below 50k → 10Y yield breaks 4.25% support, falls toward 4.10-4.15%, TLT rallies 1.5-2.5%, USD weakens 0.4-0.6% on DXY, gold pushes new highs above $4,400/oz GLD-equivalent, NVDA/AMD/AVGO get bid as duration trade comes back online → if print prints hot above 90k → 10Y reverses to 4.45-4.50%, TLT cracks $84 support, regional banks (KRE) catch bid, XLK gives back 1-2% on multiple compression → concurrent risk: a dovish miss combined with a hot wage component (AHE >+0.4% MoM) creates the worst outcome — yields up AND growth slowing, classic stagflation tape, defensive sectors XLP/XLU outperform.
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US-only print but global reverberation: a sub-50k print accelerates ECB cut path expectation given US Fed leadership effect, weakens USD against EUR/JPY, supports EM currencies (BRL, MXN). Hot print hardens DXY, pressures EM FX (TRY, IDR, INR particularly oil-sensitive).
macro_events.historical_analog: March 2025 print of 175k vs 200k consensus saw 10Y -8bp on day, NQ +1.4%, TLT +1.2%; the persistent move was 5-day duration outperformance. April 2024 print of 175k vs 240k consensus was followed by an 11bp 10Y rally over the next week.
macro_events.counterargument: ADP private payrolls earlier this week were stronger than expected, suggesting the BLS print may surprise to the upside (90k+); seasonal adjustment factors in April have produced upside surprises 6 of last 10 years. A hot print weakens the entire long-duration trade thesis and forces a tactical rotation back into financials and small-caps.

macro_events.title: Q1 earnings tape bifurcating sharply: AI/cybersec winners, tariff-exposed durables losers
macro_events.causal_chain: Yesterday after-hours produced cleanly polarized prints: Fortinet +24% on raised FY revenue and $1.85B Q1 beat → confirms enterprise security spend is non-discretionary even in capex tightening cycle → DoorDash +10% on order forecast above the high end → consumer services delivery demand inflecting positive → Whirlpool -16% after slashing FY25 EPS guide from $6 to $3-3.50 and revenue from $15.3-15.6B to ~$15B → tariff cost pass-through is failing in mid-tier durables, demand destruction is showing up in real numbers → market translates this into cleaner short-list of broken names: WHR, GE Appliances peers, LEG, MAS, FBHS — and bid for AI capex/cybersec/services delivery: NVDA, AVGO, FTNT, PANW, CRWD, DASH.
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US-tariff-exposure is the wedge: companies with majority Chinese/Mexican manufacturing footprint and limited pricing power are getting punished disproportionately; companies with pricing power (essential services, AI infra) are being rewarded.
macro_events.historical_analog: 2019 trade war Q2 prints had similar bifurcation: capital goods (DE, CAT) and home products got crushed while software/cloud (CRM, ADBE, MSFT) outperformed by 800-1200 bps in the back half. The polarization compounded for two quarters before converging.
macro_events.counterargument: If China-US tariff truce is extended past August 2026 deadline, the broken-durables names mean-revert violently — WHR could rally 25-30% on a single positive headline; risk-reward for shorting tariff-exposed industrials is asymmetric to the upside.
